name: Buttermilk Fried Chicken Sandwich
recipeText:
Yield:
6 sandwiches
Portion Size:
1 sandwich per serving
Cuisine / Style:
American / Southern-inspired casual
Primary Test Focus:
• brine logic
• frying yield
• breading pickup
• sauce application
• holding degradation
• allergen detection
Allergen Flags:
Milk/dairy, wheat/gluten, eggs if using egg-enriched buns, possible soy depending on oil/bun label
--------------------------------------------------
INGREDIENTS
--------------------------------------------------
Chicken:
Boneless skinless chicken thighs – 2.5 lb
Buttermilk Brine:
Buttermilk – 2 cups
Kosher salt – 1 Tbsp
Hot sauce – 2 Tbsp
Garlic powder – 1 tsp
Paprika – 1 tsp
Black pepper – 1/2 tsp
Breading:
All-purpose flour – 2 cups
Cornstarch – 1/2 cup
Kosher salt – 1 Tbsp
Paprika – 1 Tbsp
Garlic powder – 1 tsp
Onion powder – 1 tsp
Black pepper – 1 tsp
Cayenne – 1/2 tsp
For Frying:
Neutral frying oil – as needed
Sandwich Build:
Brioche or potato buns – 6 each
Pickle chips – 18 each
Shredded lettuce – 3 cups
Spicy mayo – 3/4 cup
--------------------------------------------------
METHOD
--------------------------------------------------
1. Trim chicken thighs into 6 even sandwich portions.
2. Combine buttermilk, salt, hot sauce, garlic powder, paprika, and black pepper.
3. Add chicken to brine and refrigerate 4–12 hours.
4. Combine flour, cornstarch, salt, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and cayenne.
5. Remove chicken from brine, allowing excess to drip off.
6. Dredge chicken in breading mix, pressing firmly to coat.
7. Rest breaded chicken on a rack for 10–15 minutes.
8. Fry at 325–350°F until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
9. Drain on rack. Do not stack.
10. Toast buns if desired.
11. Build each sandwich with bun, spicy mayo, fried chicken, pickles, lettuce, and top bun.
--------------------------------------------------
SCALING / AI TEST NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Buttermilk brine salt must remain functional but should not blindly scale too high in large batches.
• Breading does not equal edible yield. Breading pickup and leftover dredge must be accounted for separately.
• Frying oil is process fat and should not scale linearly by serving count.
• Spicy mayo is a finishing sauce and should scale by portion application.
--------------------------------------------------
FOOD SAFETY / HOLDING NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Chicken must reach 165°F internal temperature.
• Hold fried chicken on racks to preserve crispness.
• Do not cover tightly or breading will soften.
• Discard used brine.
• Avoid cross-contact between raw chicken and ready-to-eat sandwich components.

name: Smoked BBQ Pulled Pork Sliders
recipeText:
Yield:
6 servings

2 sliders per serving
12 sliders total
Cuisine / Style:
American BBQ
Primary Test Focus:
• raw-to-cooked pork yield
• long cook shrinkage
• sauce absorption
• holding moisture
• AP vs EP purchasing
• topping vs garnish logic
Allergen Flags:
Wheat/gluten depending on slider buns, possible soy depending on BBQ sauce, egg/dairy depending on slaw dressing
--------------------------------------------------
INGREDIENTS
--------------------------------------------------
Pulled Pork:
Pork shoulder / pork butt – 4 lb raw
Kosher salt – 1 Tbsp
Brown sugar – 2 Tbsp
Paprika – 1 Tbsp
Black pepper – 1 tsp
Garlic powder – 1 tsp
Onion powder – 1 tsp
Mustard powder – 1 tsp
Cayenne – 1/4 tsp
Cooking Liquid:
Apple cider vinegar – 1/2 cup
Apple juice – 1/2 cup
Sauce:
BBQ sauce – 1 cup
Reserved pork cooking juices – as needed
Slaw:
Green cabbage, shredded – 4 cups
Carrot, shredded – 1 cup
Mayonnaise – 1/2 cup
Apple cider vinegar – 2 Tbsp
Sugar – 1 Tbsp
Kosher salt – 1/2 tsp
Black pepper – 1/4 tsp
Slider Build:
Slider buns – 12 each
Pickle chips – 24 each
--------------------------------------------------
METHOD
--------------------------------------------------
1. Combine salt, brown sugar, paprika, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, mustard powder, and cayenne.
2. Rub pork shoulder evenly with spice mixture.
3. Cook pork using smoker, oven, or covered roasting method at 250–275°F until tender and pullable, approximately 195–205°F internal.
4. Rest pork 20–30 minutes.
5. Pull pork and remove excess fat or connective tissue.
6. Moisten pulled pork with reserved cooking juices.
7. Add BBQ sauce gradually until pork is coated but not drowned.
8. Combine cabbage, carrot, mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper for slaw.
9. Build sliders with pulled pork, slaw, and pickles.
--------------------------------------------------
SCALING / AI TEST NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Pork shoulder yield after cooking is commonly 55–65%.
• BBQ sauce is a coating/holding sauce, not a soup base.
• Slaw is a substantial topping and should scale by sandwich count, not garnish logic.
• Spice rub scaling should control cayenne and salt at larger batch sizes.
--------------------------------------------------
FOOD SAFETY / HOLDING NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Cook pork until tender and safe.
• Hot hold pulled pork above 135°F.
• Cool in shallow pans if cooking ahead.
• Reheat to 165°F if cooled.
• Slaw must remain cold at 41°F or below.

recipeText:

--------------------------------------------------
INGREDIENTS
--------------------------------------------------

Ground turkey – 2.5 lb
Yellow onion, finely diced – 1 cup
Garlic, minced – 1 Tbsp
Breadcrumbs – 1 cup
Milk – 1/2 cup
Eggs – 2 each
Worcestershire sauce – 1 Tbsp
Kosher salt – 2 tsp
Black pepper – 1 tsp
Dried thyme – 1 tsp
Paprika – 1 tsp
Tomato Glaze:
Ketchup – 1/2 cup
Tomato paste – 2 Tbsp
Brown sugar – 1 Tbsp
Apple cider vinegar – 1 Tbsp
Dijon mustard – 1 tsp
--------------------------------------------------
METHOD
--------------------------------------------------
1. Preheat oven to 350°F.
2. Combine breadcrumbs and milk. Let hydrate for 5 minutes.
3. Mix ground turkey, onion, garlic, hydrated breadcrumbs, eggs, Worcestershire, salt, pepper, thyme, and paprika.
4. Mix gently until combined. Do not overwork.
5. Shape into a loaf on a lined sheet pan or place into a loaf pan.
6. Combine ketchup, tomato paste, brown sugar, vinegar, and Dijon mustard.
7. Brush half the glaze over meatloaf.
8. Bake until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
9. Brush with remaining glaze during the final 10–15 minutes of cooking.
10. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
--------------------------------------------------
SCALING / AI TEST NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Binder must scale structurally, but liquid may need adjustment based on meat moisture.
• Tomato glaze is a finishing glaze and should not scale as if it is a sauce pool.
• Turkey is lean and requires moisture management.
• Over-scaling salt or Worcestershire can dominate.
--------------------------------------------------
FOOD SAFETY / HOLDING NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Ground turkey must reach 165°F.
• Rest before slicing.
• If cooling, slice after cooling only if needed and cool in shallow portions.
• Reheat to 165°F.

name: Mac And Cheese With Toasted Breadcrumbs
recipeText:
Yield:
6 servings
Portion Size:
Approximately 8 oz per serving
Cuisine / Style:
American comfort / baked pasta
Primary Test Focus:
• cheese sauce emulsion
• roux scaling
• pasta absorption
• baked holding behavior
• fat/water balance
Allergen Flags:
Milk/dairy, wheat/gluten
--------------------------------------------------
INGREDIENTS
--------------------------------------------------
Pasta:
Elbow macaroni or cavatappi, dry – 1 lb
Kosher salt for pasta water – as needed
Cheese Sauce:
Butter – 4 Tbsp
All-purpose flour – 4 Tbsp
Whole milk – 3 cups
Heavy cream – 1 cup
Sharp cheddar, shredded – 2 cups
Monterey Jack, shredded – 1 cup
Cream cheese – 4 oz
Kosher salt – 1 1/2 tsp
Dijon mustard – 1 tsp
Garlic powder – 1/2 tsp
Onion powder – 1/2 tsp
Black pepper – 1/4 tsp
Topping:
Panko breadcrumbs – 1 cup
Melted butter – 2 Tbsp
Paprika – 1/2 tsp
--------------------------------------------------
METHOD
--------------------------------------------------
1. Preheat oven to 350°F.
2. Cook pasta in salted water until just under al dente.
3. Drain pasta and reserve.
4. Melt butter in a pot.
5. Add flour and cook 1–2 minutes to form roux.
6. Slowly whisk in milk and cream.
7. Simmer until lightly thickened.
8. Reduce heat and add cheddar, Monterey Jack, and cream cheese.
9. Stir until smooth.
10. Season with salt, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper.
11. Fold pasta into cheese sauce.
12. Transfer to baking dish.
13. Toss panko with melted butter and paprika.
14. Top pasta with breadcrumbs.
15. Bake until hot and lightly browned, 20–25 minutes.
--------------------------------------------------
SCALING / AI TEST NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Cheese sauce must maintain water/fat balance.
• Pasta continues absorbing sauce during baking and holding.
• Roux and cheese cannot be scaled without checking sauce viscosity.
• Breadcrumb topping is a finishing texture and should not become too thick at scale.
--------------------------------------------------
FOOD SAFETY / HOLDING NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Hold hot above 135°F.
• If cooling, cool in shallow pans.
• Reheat gently with added milk if sauce tightens.
• Avoid overbaking before hot hold.

INGREDIENTS

Pork:

Marinade:
Achiote paste – 3 Tbsp
Guajillo chile puree – 1/2 cup
Pineapple juice – 1/2 cup
Orange juice – 1/4 cup
White vinegar – 2 Tbsp

White onion, grated or blended – 1/2 cup

METHOD

name: Chicken Piccata
recipeText:

• pan sauce emulsion
• lemon/caper intensity
• reduction logic
• flour dredge pickup
• service timing

Allergen Flags:
Wheat/gluten, milk/dairy if using butter
--------------------------------------------------
INGREDIENTS
--------------------------------------------------
Chicken:
Boneless skinless chicken breast – 3 lb
Kosher salt – 2 tsp
Black pepper – 1 tsp
All-purpose flour – 1 cup
Olive oil – 1/4 cup
Butter – 4 Tbsp
Piccata Sauce:
Dry white wine – 1 cup
Chicken stock – 1.5 cups
Lemon juice – 1/3 cup
Capers, drained – 1/4 cup
Butter, cold diced – 6 Tbsp
Parsley, chopped – 1/4 cup
For Service:
Lemon slices – 6 each
--------------------------------------------------
METHOD
--------------------------------------------------
1. Portion chicken into 6 even cutlets.
2. Pound lightly to even thickness.
3. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
4. Dredge lightly in flour and shake off excess.
5. Heat olive oil and butter in sauté pans.
6. Sear chicken until golden and cooked through.
7. Remove chicken and hold warm.
8. Deglaze pan with white wine.
9. Reduce wine by about half.
10. Add chicken stock, lemon juice, and capers.

13. Return chicken to sauce briefly or spoon sauce over chicken.
14. Finish with chopped parsley and lemon slices.

--------------------------------------------------
• Flour dredge is process coating, not total edible yield.
• Lemon juice and capers are high-impact ingredients and require control at scale.
• Butter is part of the sauce emulsion and cannot be scaled blindly without checking water/fat balance.
• Wine reduction changes concentration and acidity.
• Sauce volume should be enough to coat, not drown.
--------------------------------------------------
FOOD SAFETY / HOLDING NOTES
--------------------------------------------------
• Chicken must reach 165°F.
• Piccata sauce can break if held too hot.
• Best served quickly after sauce is mounted with butter.
• If holding, keep sauce warm but not boiling.

--------------------------------------------------
INGREDIENTS
--------------------------------------------------
Chocolate Filling:
Dark chocolate, 60–70%, chopped – 12 oz
Glucose syrup – 3 oz
Invert sugar – 2 oz
Heavy cream – 4 oz
Unsalted butter, soft – 2 oz
Cocoa butter – 1 oz
Kosher salt – pinch
Optional Flavoring:
Vanilla extract – 1/2 tsp
Liqueur – 1 Tbsp, optional
For Shelling:
Tempered chocolate shells – 30 each
--------------------------------------------------
METHOD
--------------------------------------------------
1. Place chopped chocolate and cocoa butter in a bowl.
2. Heat cream, glucose syrup, invert sugar, and salt until steaming.
3. Pour hot liquid over chocolate and cocoa butter.
4. Let sit 1 minute.
5. Stir from center outward to create emulsion.
6. Add soft butter and optional flavoring.
7. Emulsify with immersion blender while avoiding excess air.
8. Cool filling to appropriate piping temperature.
9. Pipe into tempered chocolate shells.
10. Allow filling to crystallize.
11. Cap bonbons with tempered chocolate.
